name: Audience Adaptation Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any audience adaptation task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any audience adaptation task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen audience adaptation approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. Keep audience adaptation changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Prefer explicit, readable audience adaptation solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. Validate audience adaptation outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. State assumptions about audience adaptation explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to audience adaptation (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep audience adaptation outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Document any non-obvious audience adaptation decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Before starting audience adaptation work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop audience adaptation edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of audience adaptation correctness.
- Do not skip documenting audience adaptation assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for audience adaptation, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
